input.summary:
Flat 1W front room furnished in parts/room-7.mjs: oak-stair sofa on the west wall, oriel window seat (stairs facing the room) as focal piece, dark-oak table with standing lantern, one chair, a two-high-with-pots cupboard on the north wall beside the doorway, and two hanging lanterns plus a floor lantern.
Lane x 7 from the doorway to the window seat stays clear. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; this part reported 18 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. mcd room says OK: 54 of 55 cells reachable, min light 8, no dark or dim cells.
Looked at room.png (from above and inside): it reads as a sitting room with the window seat as focal point.
left: No rug: the palette has no carpet, and a wool block on the floor would cut the walk. The floor is the shell's to change if a rug is wanted.
No bed, bookcase or barrel: none of them is in palette.json, so the shelves are a cupboard with flower pots.

mcd room counts the flower-pot tops at (4,16,12) and (11,16,12) as floor cells the walker can't reach (55 floor cells, 54 reached), though it still says OK. The room is walkable; the count is a quirk of the check.
plan.md and elements.md have no per-room checklist line for this part, so nothing was ticked. The 'Light: all rooms >= 8' element is met for this room only.
mcd check on the whole build reports 8 orphan blocks in other parts (shopfront slabs at z 17, roof slabs at y 31, sandstone at y 21). None are from this part.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell from the plan grid, then drew it as four y-layers of text for layers().
waste.cost: About 4 layer rows of 7 strings, plus one retry for the floor-level lantern and the cupboard tops, which took two build and check passes.
waste.tool: mcd plan could print a per-y template with a legend slot per room (for example a `furnish` scaffold with the floor, walls and doorway as '.'), so the layers() call starts from the room's real shape.

waste.what: Chose the lantern spots by reading the room's light map by eye, then moved one lantern after the first check said 5 cells were dim.
waste.cost: One extra make.sh and room check round, about 20 seconds.
waste.tool: mcd room's lantern-spot list already names the cell. A `--apply` flag that writes the suggested lantern into a copy of the generator would have saved the second round.

waste.what: Fixed the cupboard top and the pot cells by hand after the room check counted them as unreachable floor.
waste.tool: mcd room should skip the top of a non-full block (a flower pot, a slab) as a floor cell, so the 54-of-55 count matches the real walk.

companions.task: Place the light on the wall lantern and the floor lantern, and confirm the room reads lit after dusk from the window.
Make a rug and cushions, but only if the palette allows carpet or wool that doesn't block the walk.

structured_output.summary:
Flat 1W front room furnished in parts/room-7.mjs: oak-stair sofa on the west wall, oriel window seat (stairs facing the room) as focal piece, dark-oak table with standing lantern, one chair, a two-high-with-pots cupboard on the north wall beside the doorway, and two hanging lanterns plus a floor lantern.
Lane x 7 from the doorway to the window seat stays clear. make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; this part reported 18 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. mcd room says OK: 54 of 55 cells reachable, min light 8, no dark or dim cells.
Looked at room.png (from above and inside): it reads as a sitting room with the window seat as focal point.
left: No rug: the palette has no carpet, and a wool block on the floor would cut the walk. The floor is the shell's to change if a rug is wanted.
No bed, bookcase or barrel: none of them is in palette.json, so the shelves are a cupboard with flower pots.

mcd room counts the flower-pot tops at (4,16,12) and (11,16,12) as floor cells the walker can't reach (55 floor cells, 54 reached), though it still says OK. The room is walkable; the count is a quirk of the check.
plan.md and elements.md have no per-room checklist line for this part, so nothing was ticked. The 'Light: all rooms >= 8' element is met for this room only.
mcd check on the whole build reports 8 orphan blocks in other parts (shopfront slabs at z 17, roof slabs at y 31, sandstone at y 21). None are from this part.

waste.what: Worked out the furniture cell by cell from the plan grid, then drew it as four y-layers of text for layers().
waste.cost: About 4 layer rows of 7 strings, plus one retry for the floor-level lantern and the cupboard tops, which took two build and check passes.
waste.tool: mcd plan could print a per-y template with a legend slot per room (for example a `furnish` scaffold with the floor, walls and doorway as '.'), so the layers() call starts from the room's real shape.

waste.what: Chose the lantern spots by reading the room's light map by eye, then moved one lantern after the first check said 5 cells were dim.
waste.cost: One extra make.sh and room check round, about 20 seconds.
waste.tool: mcd room's lantern-spot list already names the cell. A `--apply` flag that writes the suggested lantern into a copy of the generator would have saved the second round.

waste.what: Fixed the cupboard top and the pot cells by hand after the room check counted them as unreachable floor.
waste.tool: mcd room should skip the top of a non-full block (a flower pot, a slab) as a floor cell, so the 54-of-55 count matches the real walk.
